correctness.rationale: Bao's full arXiv v1 was inspected. Theorem 1.3(a) gives the rank sum, part (b) requires the square root of A for the first outer summand, part (c)(i) has exactly one of the square roots of A and C in the CM field, and part (d) requires the square root of C for the third outer summand. Hence a middle rank-one contribution of type (c)(i) forces one outer rank to vanish. In Bao's Example 6.3, the paper itself states that the square root of C is absent but nevertheless concludes that the third rank is one, so the printed example is inconsistent with its own theorem. Independently reconstructed algebra gives the component ranks (1,1,0). Fresh symbolic algebra also reproduced the discriminant cube identities and verified both displayed sections.

That is a motivated structural boundary and correction.

correctness.rationale: Bao's stated rank criteria force the total rank to be at most two whenever the middle rank-one contribution is from case (c)(i). For the printed Example 6.3 parameters, exact algebra gives component ranks (1,1,0); the first outer cube condition and the middle cube identities hold, while the third outer square-root condition fails. The nonsquare claim for m is proved modulo 8, and symbolic substitution verifies the two displayed sections.
